nodes.label: Event Collision Suffix Rule
nodes.rationale: Angular Kigumi wrappers strip the wa- prefix and camelCase event names; when the resulting name collides with a DOM property or component method (e.g. wa-show vs show(), blur vs DOM blur), an Event suffix is appended to avoid collision (e.g. showEvent, blurEvent, inputEvent).

nodes.label: Hoisted Dropdown Pattern (z-index escape)
nodes.rationale: Use the hoist prop when Dropdown is inside an overflow-constrained container (Card, Dialog, Drawer, Details, table cells) because hoisting teleports the dropdown panel to the body, escaping overflow:hidden and z-index stacking contexts.

nodes.label: Automatic Focus Management / Focus Trap
nodes.rationale: Dialog and Drawer handle focus automatically (move to first focusable element on open, trap tab cycling while open, return focus to trigger on close), so no manual focus management or .focus() calls are needed.

nodes.label: requestClose() vs hide() Pattern
nodes.rationale: requestClose() should always be preferred over hide() when programmatically closing overlays because requestClose() fires the cancelable wa-hide event (allowing interception, e.g. unsaved-changes warnings), while hide() bypasses the event lifecycle entirely.

nodes.label: Tier System (Free/Pro Detection)
nodes.rationale: package.json is single source of truth for tier (installed package), not config, because config can be edited freely but the installed package reflects reality; fallback to token detection via env var, npmrc, or .env in priority order.

nodes.label: Two-tier memory strategy (Tier 1 persistent / Tier 2 live status)
nodes.norm_label: two-tier memory strategy (tier 1 persistent / tier 2 live status)

nodes.label: CSS Cascade Layers token override pattern
nodes.norm_label: css cascade layers token override pattern
nodes.rationale: Override --wa-* custom properties in src/styles/theme.css; CSS Cascade Layers ensure overrides win automatically without needing !important.

nodes.label: Shared theme package (@repo/theme)
nodes.rationale: layers.css stays per-workspace because it's tied to the WA package version and tier; only theme.css is shared since it is preserved on kigumi init re-runs, so the import from @repo/theme won't be overwritten.

nodes.label: Pro shim content restriction (names/types/signatures only, no docs prose)
nodes.norm_label: pro shim content restriction (names/types/signatures only, no docs prose)
nodes.rationale: Web Awesome Pro is commercial software whose license permits a seat holder to use it but forbids handing Pro assets to people without a license, and this repository is public. The generator drops documentation prose from Pro's type definitions and keeps only names, types, and signatures, which are the interface templates must compile against.

nodes.label: Why Pro is not a real npm dependency
nodes.norm_label: why pro is not a real npm dependency
nodes.rationale: Pro requires a paid WEBAWESOME_NPM_TOKEN; adding it to package.json would force every contributor and CI runner to have the token or fail pnpm install. Instead the shim provides accurate Pro types committed to the repo, generated on the maintainer's machine.

nodes.label: Pro shim maintainer regeneration workflow (9 steps)
nodes.norm_label: pro shim maintainer regeneration workflow (9 steps)
nodes.rationale: Temporarily authenticates to the Pro npm registry, installs Pro locally, regenerates the shim from Pro's real .d.ts files, then reverts package manifests and removes the local install so Pro never becomes a real committed dependency.

nodes.norm_label: phase 5 angular skills + docs design spec

nodes.label: Angular Event Collision Suffix Convention
nodes.rationale: Angular outputs use (outputName) syntax; native DOM event names that collide with Angular's own event bindings (blur, focus, show, input) are suffixed (blurEvent, focusEvent, showEvent, inputEvent) to avoid ambiguity between the native DOM event and the wrapped custom output.

nodes.label: React Event Naming (wa-hide -> onHide)
nodes.rationale: Event handler names are derived from templates, not from a naive WA-event-to-camelCase transform: wa-hide maps to onHide, not the literal onWaHide, so consumers get idiomatic React prop names for custom events.

nodes.label: Next.js as a React Variant
nodes.rationale: Next.js (App Router and Pages Router, with or without src/) reuses React templates rather than adding a 'next' framework enum value, to avoid duplicating 84 components under templates/nextjs/ for no gain. Detected via isNextProject/detectNextRouter/detectSourceLayout in src/utils/detect-framework.ts.

nodes.label: Next.js Pages Router CSS Policy
nodes.rationale: Next forbids global CSS imports outside pages/_app.tsx, so Kigumi omits layers.css import from generated lib/kigumi.ts and strips per-component CSS imports when Pages Router is detected.

nodes.label: docs/.npmrc token generation rationale
nodes.rationale: pnpm does not use global ~/.npmrc auth for scoped registries, so the token must be in the project .npmrc. The gitignored docs/.npmrc file is generated by pnpm run setup:npmrc from .env, checked in priority order: WEBAWESOME_NPM_TOKEN env var, global ~/.npmrc, docs/.env, then root .env.

nodes.label: Fork PR secret-skip rationale
nodes.rationale: The docs site depends on the paid Web Awesome Pro package. Pull requests from forks do not receive repository secrets, so installing the Pro package would hit Cloudsmith with an empty token and fail with a 401 on an ordinary contribution. CI detects missing WEBAWESOME_NPM_TOKEN and skips docs/storybook/chromatic steps instead of failing.

nodes.label: Full-CI matrix gating rationale
nodes.rationale: React 18-vs-19 differences are JSX-typing only and well-bounded; starter coverage for non-react frameworks is high-value only when templates or deps change. Bugs missed on a regular PR get caught at the next release PR (full-ci auto-fires on changeset-release/main) before publish. So matrix expands to full coverage only when the 'full-ci' label is present, the branch is changeset-release/main, or (starter only) templates/deps changed.

nodes.label: Dark Mode Inversion Rule
nodes.rationale: Dark mode is a COLOR INVERSION of the same visual identity, not a new design direction; structural tokens (radius, spacing, fonts, line-heights, shadow scales, transitions) must never change between modes, only colors.

nodes.label: CSS Parts (::part()) Styling
nodes.rationale: There are no --wa-button-*/--wa-input-*/--wa-card-* component-specific tokens; individual component internals must be styled via ::part() selectors, keeping Shadow DOM internals out of the public custom-property API.

nodes.label: Web Awesome 7-Layer CSS Cascade
nodes.rationale: Uses a 7-layer cascade (wa-native < wa-utilities < wa-color-palette < wa-color-variant < wa-theme < wa-theme-dimension < wa-theme-overrides) so user overrides always win at the highest-priority layer without needing !important.

nodes.label: Web Awesome Scale Tokens
nodes.rationale: Scale tokens (--wa-font-size-scale, --wa-space-scale, --wa-border-radius-scale, etc.) act as global multipliers so a single override cascades proportionally to every derived token in that category, avoiding per-token edits.

nodes.label: @layer wa-theme-overrides
nodes.rationale: Highest-priority cascade layer where all custom CSS should live so overrides win by cascade order rather than by !important, keeping specificity predictable.

nodes.label: tests/unit/schemas/ directory (Cluster T fast-check + corrupt-config tests)

nodes.label: tests/unit/regression/ directory (Cluster V bug-bash suite)
nodes.rationale: Provides documented evidence that the test suite catches specific historical breakage that real users hit, distinct from mutation testing which measures generic breakage detection.

nodes.label: Regression test file-header contract (Protects/Bug/Fix)
nodes.rationale: Every regression test opens with a header naming the protected PR/F-ID, the user-visible bug, and the fix commit SHA, so a failing test is immediately traceable back to the historical issue it guards.

nodes.label: Regression entry revert-verification workflow (scratch branch + git revert)
nodes.norm_label: regression entry revert-verification workflow (scratch branch + git revert)
nodes.rationale: Verifies a new regression test actually fails when the original fix is reverted, proving the test catches the specific historical breakage; if git revert is impossible due to later refactors, the logical invariant is asserted instead and noted as manual code rollback.

nodes.label: Three-way merge (Base / Yours / Theirs)
nodes.rationale: Kigumi's biggest advantage over copy-paste workflows: customize components freely, then safely pull in template improvements without manual diffing. Base is the .kigumi/snapshots/ original template output, Yours is the current customized file, Theirs is what the current CLI would generate fresh; comparing all three tells which changes are yours vs. the template's.

nodes.label: State-File Staleness Review (14-day window)
nodes.rationale: Initiatives whose state-file has not been touched in 14+ days are surfaced for a manual 'still accurate?' check, because state-files drift out of sync with reality over time and a periodic freshness sweep catches stale status claims before they mislead release-readiness or triage decisions.

nodes.label: 3-Criteria New-Finding Rule (K1/K2/K3)
nodes.rationale: A finding is tracked as a formal Issue only if all three hold: (K1) not fixable in the current PR, (K2) blocks v0.20.0 release confidence, an active feature, or test-layer completeness, and (K3) at least medium severity. This graduated rule prevents backlog bloat from low-value findings while ensuring release-blocking or feature-blocking issues are never silently dropped -- findings failing K1/K2 become PR-description notes instead, and findings failing K3 are acknowledged but not tracked.

nodes.label: Web Awesome Sync Chain
nodes.rationale: custom-elements.json -> parse-custom-elements.ts -> component-metadata.ts (auto-generated) -> registry.ts (hand-maintained) -> templates/**/*.hbs; registry is source of truth for the CLI, metadata is supplementary.

nodes.label: Templates-First Development
nodes.rationale: Never edit generated code; always update templates/ since they are real framework source files validated by tsc and eslint, and the CLI only substitutes the Free->Pro tier import path at runtime.

nodes.label: Templates converted from Handlebars to real source files
nodes.norm_label: templates converted from handlebars to real source files
nodes.rationale: Tier substitution moved from Handlebars.compile() to a single String.replaceAll regex inside materializeTemplate(), enabling tsc/eslint to cover templates/** and catch authoring mistakes at PR time instead of on user machines.

nodes.label: The One Rule That Matters Most (never edit generated code)
nodes.norm_label: the one rule that matters most (never edit generated code)
nodes.rationale: Hand-editing a generated wrapper gets silently overwritten by the next generation run and CI flags the drift; correct loop is edit templates/, pnpm build, validate.

nodes.label: CSS Cascade Layers (base < theme)
nodes.rationale: Later layers always override earlier layers regardless of specificity, so theme.css reliably overrides Web Awesome defaults without needing !important.

nodes.label: Path handling security scope
nodes.rationale: Registry-supplied file paths must never resolve outside the registry root or write outside the target project; both registry schema and fetch layer must guard against traversal.

nodes.label: Templates-First Architecture
nodes.rationale: Wrappers live as real framework source files under templates/{react,vue,angular}/{Component}/; the CLI reads them at install time and applies a single substitution (Free->Pro tier swap on the @awesome.me/webawesome import path), keeping generated output deterministic for the three-way merge system.

nodes.label: ControlValueAccessor (CVA) Pattern
nodes.rationale: Kigumi Angular wrappers for form components implement ControlValueAccessor so they work natively with Angular's forms system via [(ngModel)] or [formControl], avoiding manual event wiring.

nodes.label: Studio state flow (setProperty -> getStyleObject -> preview style)
nodes.norm_label: studio state flow (setproperty -> getstyleobject -> preview style)

nodes.label: Theme-flash prevention inline script
nodes.rationale: Sets the color scheme before first paint to avoid a light/dark flash. Reads the same localStorage key as ThemeContext ('theme-preference'); defaults to the system setting via matchMedia. Must stay inline and blocking so it runs before the CSS loads.

nodes.label: Studio isolation guard rails
nodes.rationale: Never modify existing ThemeContext (use separate StudioContext instead) and never import Kigumi Studio CSS into Landing Page styles, to maintain preview isolation so the Studio theme does not leak into the Landing Page. Also mirrors global Kigumi rules: class not className, declare global not declare module 'react', no !important, no any type, always use @/components/ui wrappers instead of raw wa-* elements.

nodes.label: npm provenance disabled rationale
nodes.rationale: id-token: write would let npm attach a provenance attestation, but npm only verifies provenance for public source repos; this repo is private, so publishing stays unsigned until that changes.

nodes.label: PAT pre-flight check rationale
nodes.rationale: Fail fast with an actionable message instead of dying deep inside changesets/action with 'not all refs are readable' when the PAT is expired, rotated, or missing the pull-requests scope. Checkout uses the default GITHUB_TOKEN (always has repo access) while PERSONAL_GITHUB_TOKEN is required only for PR creation and is validated early.

nodes.label: Pack destination outside workspace rationale
nodes.rationale: Pack into RUNNER_TEMP, never the workspace: a stray *.tgz in the repo root gets swept into the release commit by changesets/action's `git add .`. --pack-destination prints the absolute tarball path.

nodes.label: --components-dir explicit path rationale
nodes.rationale: Explicit --components-dir pins the assertion path independent of kigumi's sourceLayout detection (which requires more than just an empty src/ dir to default to src/components/ui).

nodes.label: Built-In Responsiveness Principle
nodes.rationale: Web Awesome layout utilities (.wa-grid auto-fit/minmax, .wa-flank auto-stack via --content-percentage) are inherently responsive so @media queries are rarely needed; they're reserved for hiding elements, changing layout primitive, font-size adjustments, and fixed positioning.

nodes.label: wa-flank Full-Height Sidebar Rule
nodes.rationale: `.wa-flank` sidebar layouts need `wa-align-items-stretch` for full-height sidebars; without it the sidebar is vertically centered instead of stretching to fill the container.

nodes.label: Native DOM Events Rule (Forms)
nodes.rationale: Form controls emit NATIVE DOM events, NOT CustomEvent -- flagged as the #1 agent mistake with Kigumi forms; overlay components use CustomEvent instead, creating a two-mode event model across the library.

nodes.label: CustomEvent Rule (Overlays)
nodes.rationale: Overlays emit CustomEvent (wa-show, wa-hide), NOT native DOM events -- the opposite convention from form controls, so agents must not conflate the two event models.

nodes.label: Framework-Agnostic Layer Concept
nodes.rationale: Web Awesome's HTML, CSS, slot names, and atomic Kigumi component imports are identical across React/Vue/Angular and copy verbatim; only wrapper code (state, effects, events, control flow, refs) needs translation, so the cross-framework skill focuses solely on mapping source-to-target idioms rather than redocumenting target conventions.

nodes.label: coverageAnalysis: 'all' (Stryker config choice)
nodes.rationale: Chosen instead of spec's 'perTest' preference because the patched @stryker-mutator/vitest-runner@9.6.1 plus vitest 4.x hangs the perTest dry run regardless of mutate scope; 'all' is functionally equivalent for the score since it runs all tests per mutant and the kill criterion is the same.

nodes.label: disableTypeChecks: 'src/**/*.ts' (Stryker config choice)
nodes.rationale: Stryker's mutators intentionally introduce type errors; treating them as failures would pollute the mutation score. Type safety is enforced separately by pnpm type-check and pnpm check:tests (Cluster Q1's tests baseline).

nodes.norm_label: mutation testing (pnpm test:mutation, cluster v f-x10)
nodes.rationale: StrykerJS mutates a declared subset of src/** and runs the unit suite per mutant; break threshold 80%. V1 baseline scope is src/utils/tier.ts only (89.13% kill rate) due to two upstream blockers tracked in stryker.conf.mjs.

nodes.label: Negative-Path Inventory table (Cluster T / PR-T3)
nodes.rationale: Every user-facing command must have at least three negative-path tests (invalid input, missing dependency, failed pre-flight, surfaced error); reviewers extending a command must add/update a row when introducing a new failure mode.

nodes.label: Patched @stryker-mutator/vitest-runner (patches/)
nodes.rationale: vitest 4.x's threads pool forbids process.chdir(), which 5 legacy unit tests rely on. The runner hardcodes pool: 'threads'; the patch switches it to pool: 'forks' (singleFork) so all tests run.

nodes.label: React className rule on Kigumi wrappers
nodes.norm_label: react classname rule on kigumi wrappers
nodes.rationale: In consumer code, always use className (not class) on both native HTML elements and Kigumi wrapper components, because the wrapper accepts className via HTMLAttributes and internally forwards it to the underlying wa-* element as class={clsx(...)}; using class directly causes TS2322. CLAUDE.md's 'class not className' rule applies only inside template/wrapper source code (templates/react/*.tsx), not to consumer usage of the generated wrappers.

nodes.label: variant="primary" -> variant="brand" mapping
nodes.rationale: Web Awesome docs/examples use variant="primary" but Kigumi's prop values do not include "primary"; it must be mapped to variant="brand" since Kigumi's canonical brand variant name differs from upstream WA docs.

nodes.label: Vue slot attribute rule (not template #name)
nodes.rationale: Kigumi Vue wrappers pass content through a single default <slot /> to the underlying web component's shadow DOM, so named slots must be targeted with the slot="name" HTML attribute rather than Vue's <template #name> syntax, which targets Vue's own (nonexistent) named slot system on the wrapper.

nodes.label: Gap classes implicitly set display:flex via :where()
nodes.norm_label: gap classes implicitly set display:flex via :where()
nodes.rationale: Gap classes set gap to the matching space token and implicitly set display: flex via a zero-specificity :where() rule, so they work on any element without conflicting with more specific author styles.

nodes.label: Align-items classes implicitly set display:flex
nodes.rationale: These classes also implicitly set display: flex so they can be applied standalone without a separate layout primitive class.

nodes.label: Pages Router owns all CSS imports (trade-off)
nodes.norm_label: pages router owns all css imports (trade-off)
nodes.rationale: Next's Pages Router enforces that global CSS can only be imported from _app.tsx directly, not transitively. Kigumi detects Pages Router at generation time and omits the layers.css import from lib/kigumi.ts and the per-component .css imports from each wrapper, so the build succeeds; the trade-off is that _app.tsx owns all CSS imports.

nodes.label: shamefully-hoist=true .npmrc fix for pnpm + Pages Router
nodes.norm_label: shamefully-hoist=true .npmrc fix for pnpm + pages router
nodes.rationale: Next's Pages Router SSR pipeline holds a single React instance, but pnpm's default isolated node_modules layout leaks multiple React resolution paths through styled-jsx and other Next dev-overlay deps, causing 'Cannot read properties of null' errors during SSR.

nodes.label: Server-rendered Web Awesome output limitation
nodes.rationale: Custom elements render as empty wa-* tags during SSR and hydrate on the client; visible output appears after hydration. This is a fundamental property of custom elements without Declarative Shadow DOM, not Kigumi-specific. Web Awesome's Pro SSR loader is the intended path for fully-server-rendered shadow output.

nodes.label: suppressHydrationWarning on host element
nodes.rationale: Lit-based Web Awesome components reflect default attributes to the DOM during connectedCallback (e.g. appearance='outlined' on wa-button). React's SSR output does not include those, so without suppression every page mounting a Kigumi component throws a hydration-mismatch warning. It suppresses only the host element and is a no-op in non-SSR contexts, so Vite projects are unaffected.

nodes.label: transpilePackages config fix for Pages Router SSR
nodes.norm_label: transpilepackages config fix for pages router ssr
nodes.rationale: Pages Router SSR uses Node ESM resolution, which does not follow pnpm's symlink graph for Lit. Without transpilePackages entries for @awesome.me/webawesome(-pro), next dev crashes with Cannot find package 'lit'.

nodes.label: 'use client' directive injection
nodes.rationale: Injected on line 1 of every generated React wrapper and of src/lib/kigumi.ts. Without it, Next would try to server-render the custom element reference and fail because Web Awesome's Lit runtime depends on browser APIs.

nodes.rationale: Each shadow dimension has its own multiplier applied to all three tiers. Defaults produce a straight-down drop shadow (offset-x-scale 0) with a negative spread-scale (-0.5) that pulls the edge inward, keeping the shadow tight against the element.

nodes.label: Vue defineModel two-way binding pattern
nodes.rationale: Kigumi wrappers are real Vue components (not raw wa-* elements). Each wrapper uses defineModel and syncs the value with the underlying web component via watch and event listeners, so you never need to manually listen to input or change events for basic data binding.

nodes.label: Vue .prop modifier for complex data
nodes.rationale: Vue serializes bound attributes to strings for raw <wa-*> elements, turning arrays/objects into "[object Object]". The .prop modifier passes data as a JS property instead. Kigumi wrappers use v-bind="props" internally so .prop is unnecessary with wrappers.

nodes.label: Vue slot="name" pattern (not <template #name>)
nodes.rationale: Web components use the HTML slot attribute, not Vue's <template #name> syntax. The slot attribute is part of the web component spec and tells the browser's Shadow DOM where to project the element; Vue's <template #name> only works with Vue components that define <slot name="..."> in their own template.

nodes.rationale: @awesome.me/webawesome is explicitly excluded from Dependabot auto-updates because Kigumi is conformant to a specific WA version tracked in src/utils/version-map.ts; bumping WA is a deliberate, coordinated effort (regenerating templates, checking for drift) rather than something safe to auto-float via a routine dependency PR.

nodes.rationale: WA 3.5.0+ marks show()/requestClose()/getMarked()/updateAll() as privacy:'private' in the CEM, so wrappers converge on the attribute-driven pattern (open prop) instead of imperative calls.

nodes.label: React 19 ref-typing fix (F-072)
nodes.rationale: React 19 ref-typing errors across 75 templates fixed via callback-ref pattern with WaXxx class type imports; removed private show/requestClose methods from Dialog/Drawer ref interface in favor of the open attribute.

nodes.rationale: Heavy CI jobs only run when relevant paths change, to stay within GitHub Actions allowance; dorny/paths-filter computes outputs consumed by gated jobs' if predicates. full-ci label and changeset-release/main branch force full matrix.

nodes.label: Mock budget (pnpm check:mocks)

nodes.label: No wa-table Component Rule
nodes.rationale: No <wa-table> component exists; use native HTML <table> with WA CSS variables for styling because a DataGrid component is planned by Web Awesome but not yet available.
